current.text: The projected starting five is Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins and Jalen Duren. It is the same five as last season.
The projected bench order is Isaiah Joe as sixth man, then Ron Holland, Paul Reed and Daniss Jenkins. Prince or Kevin Huerter gets the last rotation spot.
Last season the team used a deep 12 to 13 player rotation that limited everyone's minutes.
Isaiah Stewart is gone. Paul Reed is now the main backup big behind Duren.
As Duren's backup, Reed would play about 20 minutes a night.
Frontcourt depth behind Duren is thinner. Power forward depth is very weak unless Ausar Thompson and Ron Holland play the four.
Duren's contract situation was the big offseason question. The newest preview treats him as back and starting at center.

If Duren's situation is not settled, Paul Reed is a late flyer. A Duren trade would bring back another center, and a holdout is a worry. Analysts do not expect Detroit to start the season with Reed at center.
With Duren in the lineup, the team will still have some spacing issues.
Tobias Harris is gone, and the team has very few creators besides Cade Cunningham.
The thin creation could push Cunningham's assists up, unless Daniss Jenkins takes a bigger ball-handling role. The team may need Jenkins as another ball handler.
The plan gives Ausar Thompson and Duren on-ball roles. If that plan is failing by January, the team may trade for a secondary playmaker at the deadline.
Analysts do not trust coach J.B. Bickerstaff's latest comments on Ausar Thompson's minutes.
Detroit projects as a winning team. One expert projects 50 to 51 wins and a third or fourth seed in the East, and the win total of 49.5 ranks 6th.
The fantasy playoff schedule is 4-3-4 for our March 28 end. That is 11 games, rank 4 of 30, so it helps Detroit players in weeks 19 to 21.
The team has 15 back-to-backs, and no rest risks are expected.
There are no notable injuries on the team.

durable.text: The team is built on defense. The front office wants only enough offense, not an offensive superstar.
Coach J.B. Bickerstaff has repeatedly misled about Ausar Thompson's minutes and health, so his public comments on minutes need caution.

note: Detroit is a defense-first team that expects to win. It has a strong 4-3-4 schedule in our fantasy playoff weeks and no expected rest risk, which helps its starters. Cunningham's assists could rise because the team has few other creators. Ausar Thompson and Duren get on-ball roles, but the deep bench caps value for Joe, Huerter, Robinson and Holland. Early on, confirm that Duren is signed and starting, because Paul Reed is the main backup big. Treat Bickerstaff's comments on Thompson's minutes with caution.
